text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--- The population of Thule in northwest Greenland is to take legal action against the Danish state for its forced eviction of local eskimos in the early 1950s to make way for a U.S. military base.

--- Danish film director Lars von Trier's latest film "Breaking the Waves" has been nominated for the prestigious U.S. Golden Globe film award in two categories, best film and best actress (for Britain's Emily Watson) .

--- Scandinavia's biggest hacker court case ended with six hackers accused of breaking into computer systems at the U.S. Pentagon defence headquarters receiving community service, provisional prison sentences and fines.

--- Fishing in European waters is to be controlled by satellite in future, EU fishing ministers agreed in Brussels on Thursday, rejecting Danish opposition to the suggestion. Danish Jutland North Sea fishermen are furious about the idea and threatening to boycott the surveillance system.

--- A decision on building a fixed link across the Baltic Fehmarn Belt between south Denmark and north Germany has been postponed at least two years due to differences of opinion between the Danish and German governments.
--- Business companies' growing faith in sales in domestic and foreign markets has upped investment and more can be expected in 1997 and 1998, a new report shows.
